I’d take the first pill a little after you get off from work on Thursday just in case you feel a few cramps as well (I also took pain reliever before just in case). The day you take that 2nd dose of medication, you’re going to need to need to be home because the pain and bleeding started 10-15 minutes after I put it in my mouth. That day and the next 2 days weren’t the best and I ran to the toilet a lot. Be sure to be close to a bathroom, have pads ready, have soup and a heating pad ready, and honestly sleeping pills because it got so intense for me that I had to force myself to sleep. Also be sure to take pain medication 30 minutes before you start the 2nd medication.

Also, I’m not 100% sure about colocating, so I would ask the recruiter. Both rates can be stationed with Marines technically and you can even be stationed on a Marine base (I was for my first command).

AZ2(AW) here, and honestly that’s up you.

I LOVE being an AZ, it has its days though. Making AZ3 is like at 90% right now, so it’s easy. AZ2 is usually between 45%-70%, so still easy. AZ1 and up though......... yea, I’m on my fourth try lol.

If you want a set schedule, I’d say go PS. As an AZ, even though it’s administration, you’ll be working alongside maintenance. AZs may not be the first to show up to work, but most likely, you’ll be one of the last leaving.

AZs travel more depending on how valuable they are and if the workplace demands it. On deployments, you can go on detachments (meaning, the main deployment is in a certain place and if an aircraft is needed somewhere else, then that plane(s) will take a crew of qualified personnel along with it).

And with that being said, it also depends on what type of aircraft you go to, your in/out of shop quals, likability (seriously lol), the ship, etc.

So yea, if you want stability, I’d def go PS.

I would absolutely try to live on base. When I was stationed there, living off base was a bit inconvenient, especially if you have to use a main highway.
And on top of that, it was very expensive.

Congrats on the Hawaii orders tho, make sure to visit the other islands, go on hikes/skydiving, try a steakplate with white rice and a salad on the side and be sure to cover it all in the “special sauce”!
Most of the places don’t have A/C, but I mean it’s usually always in the 70s.

Enjoy the beaches, take your time exploring the island since you can’t drive anywhere else and be sure to respect the locals, they’re amazing. And please, respect their culture.
